g.text: Data Partitioning & Sharding: replication multiplies reads, sharding multiplies both
Same 3-node cluster, two different splits of the data
Every node holds the FULL dataset
Only reads are distributed across nodes
Every node holds 100% of the data.
Reads: distributed across 3 nodes -- read throughput scales with node count.
Writes: still bottlenecked on the primary -- adding replicas never raises
write throughput or total storage ceiling.
Each node holds only 1/3 of the dataset
Both reads AND writes are distributed
writes routed directly to the owning shard by hash(shard key) -- no shared bottleneck
Each node holds ~33% of the data.
Writes: routed by shard key -- 3x the write-throughput ceiling. Storage: 3x too.
Cost: a query needing data from >1 shard (a cross-shard join, a global scan)
must fan out to every shard and merge results -- a single node never had to do this.
Replication multiplies READ capacity. Sharding multiplies WRITE capacity and STORAGE. They solve different problems -- and can be combined (shard the data, then replicate each shard).
